subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T15:05:00Z
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements

Hi Anika (and Carlos),

Great to meet you both today - thanks for the time and for walking us through Finly's usage and constraints. Wanted to capture the highlights and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points we heard
- UX: your front-end streaming experience is intermittently choppy; users see long first-byte times and token bursts that make chat feel laggy.
- Latency spikes: p95 token latency spikes up to ~800ms under peak load (especially end-of-day batch runs).
- Throughput: concurrent active user sessions peak ~200-250, with spikes to ~350 during billing cycles.
- Cost predictability: current hosted model spend is rising without clear unit-cost visibility.

Current stack (from our call)
- Front-end: React streaming client with SSE/WebSocket; token rendering client-side.
- Model: Mixed usage of OpenAI hosted endpoints for chat generation; some on-prem rule-based fallbacks.
- Infra: Requests route through an API gateway + autoscaled app instances; no dedicated inference pool today.

Success criteria (what Finly measures)
- p95 latency: <= 300 ms for end-to-end interactive streaming (first-byte <= 200 ms preferred).
- Concurrency: support sustained 200 concurrent streaming sessions with headroom for spikes to 350.
- UX: seamless token-by-token streaming with no >1s interruptions for 99% of sessions.
- Costs: demonstrable unit-cost reduction vs current hosted spend (target: 30% reduction).

Proposed next steps
1) Tech deep-dive / perf plan (Aditya to lead) - run a small benchmark with your sample prompts and traffic profile; measure p95, start-of-stream, and steady-state token latency.
2) Share artifacts: I attached the discovery notes, our benchmark deck, and a draft SOW template.
3) POC timeline: target 3-4 week POC (week 1: infra/setup & baseline runs, week 2: tuning + caching, week 3: customer validation, week 4: wrap & SOW).
4) Commercials: we’ll ballpark Dedicated vs Hosted unit economics after the POC results.

Can we schedule the tech deep-dive with Aditya next week? He’s available Tue/Thu mornings PT. Also please upload a small set of representative prompts (and a short traffic profile) to the Drive link I included.

Thanks - excited to dig in.

Best,
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa - this is great and accurate. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 800ms p95 is what we see on average for full response latency during peak hours; token streaming first-byte is often ~300-500ms depending on model and region.
- Concurrency: 200 is accurate for normal peak; the 350 spike happens during our daily payroll generation window (about 10 minutes).
- Prompts: I'll drop a small set (~25 prompts) into the Drive folder today; they include different lengths and some large-context examples (~2k tokens).

Biggest risk for us is maintaining the streaming UX during the payroll spike - if token latency jumps, our agents report a lot of user churn. So start-of-stream (first-byte) needs to be stable under bursty concurrency.

Tech deep-dive: Tue 2026-06-16 10:00 PT works for Carlos and me. Please confirm.

-Anika
Director of Product, Finly
anika@finly.com

Hi all - quick note ahead of the deep-dive. I put together a short perf plan and required artifacts below. I’ll bring detailed test scripts to the session.

Perf plan (high level)
1) Baseline run: replay Finly’s sample prompts at current concurrency to capture end-to-end p95 and token metrics.
2) Server-side tuning: enable KV prefix caching and adaptive batching to reduce duplicate work across similar prompts. Measure p95 improvements.
3) Streaming optimizations: evaluate lower start-of-stream path (smaller initial decode chunk) + lower-latency kernels for first tokens.
4) Concurrency scaling: run sustained 200-session test with short 10-min spike to 350 to validate degradation behavior and auto-scaling policies.

Metrics to capture
- p95 first-byte latency (ms)
- p95 per-token steady-state latency (ms)
- throughput (requests/sec) and successful session rate (%)
- end-to-end time-to-first-render for client (ms)

Required artifacts from Finly
- 25 representative prompts (you mentioned you’ll upload)
- Traffic profile (concurrency, session length distribution, spike windows)
- A short sample of front-end streaming client logs (if available)

POC scaffolding notes
- Timeline: 3-4 weeks as Marissa suggested. We’ll aim to have baseline numbers in first 3 business days after access is provided.
- Environment: For speed, we’ll run in Redwood Dedicated dev pool in us-west-2 unless you have residency requirements.

I’ll attach the perf checklist and sample script in the Drive folder right after this email. Looking forward to Tuesday - I’ll demo a short benchmark run and expected tuning knobs.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
